body:
KKR & Co. Inc.(KKR) has struck a deal to acquire Gen II Fund Services LLC, a New York-based administrator for private capital funds, in a transaction valued at $5.1 billion including debt, deepening the investment firm's push into the plumbing that supports the alternative asset industry.

The purchase from Hg, General Atlantic and other minority investors was announced Monday. Hg and General Atlantic first backed Gen II in 2020, and since then the company has quadrupled revenue and EBITDA while completing four acquisitions.

Gen II provides back-office functions such as tax, compliance, treasury and technology services to private equity, private credit and other private-market managers. It serves more than 275 investment firms representing over $2 trillion in private-fund capital.

KKR plans to make the investment through its Core Private Equity strategy. Steven Millner, Gen II's co-founder and chief executive, will continue to lead the business, the buyer said.

The deal is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. KKR said it intends to support Gen II's expansion in the U.S. and overseas while investing further in proprietary technology and artificial intelligence tools.

Fund administrators have become attractive acquisition targets for private equity firms because of their reputation for generating steady and growing fee income, according to the Wall Street Journal. The business model does not depend on investment performance, making it a stable counterpart to the volatile returns of buyout funds themselves.

The transaction further expands KKR's presence in businesses that underpin private markets. In May, the firm acquired Arctos, an investment company that provides capital solutions to alternative asset managers and invests in sports franchises, in a deal initially valued at about $1.4 billion.

KKR had $5.3 billion in cash and short-term investments as of the end of the second quarter.

Wall Street analysts have largely maintained constructive views on the stock. The shares carry a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $126.82, according to data compiled by Benzinga. Wells Fargo initiated coverage on Oct. 2 with an Equal-Weight rating and a $97 price target, while Oppenheimer maintained an Outperform rating on Aug. 27 and raised its forecast to $166. Argus Research kept a Buy rating on Aug. 4 and lifted its target to $125.

KKR trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 28.7. The company is scheduled to report its next quarterly results on Nov. 9, with Wall Street projecting earnings of $1.59 per share, up from $1.41 a year earlier, and revenue of $2.80 billion compared with $2.40 billion in the year-ago period.

Exchange-traded funds with significant KKR weightings include the Tema Listed Private Managers ETF(PRVT) at 5.16%, the Akre Focus ETF(AKRE) at 7.10%, and the Invesco Global Listed Private Equity ETF(PSP) at 4.89%. Because KKR represents a meaningful position in these funds, sizable ETF flows can contribute to buying or selling pressure in the stock.
